meta.noHallucinations: NO HALLUCINATIONS IS THE RULE OF THIS PROJECT. Every price, karat, weight, policy and claim on this site was read from the linked official source page on the date shown next to it, and the session that read it is named. If a value could not be confirmed, it is left BLANK and published on the Flagged for Review page — never inferred, estimated, currency-converted or filled in from a similar listing. Derived numbers (fine-gold grams, metal value, price/metal) are computed from verified inputs and recomputed by the checker. After every review pass, run python3 scripts/verify.py.

liveCheck.method: Nine checks were re-opened live with fetch_page on 2026-10-23 (late UTC) and transcribed field by field into verification/evidence/6d10ac0a/ before any canonical value was touched. The remaining 37 checks are inherited unchanged from data/live_check_bc4e36a1.json, captured the same date, and keep their original evidence ids and paths. Two pages could only be read partially; they are logged in partialReads and upgraded nothing. No missing value was inferred, EUR was not converted to USD, no weight range was turned into an exact gram figure, and no seller statement was promoted to an assay result.
liveCheck.timeNote: Only the retrieval date is asserted for fetches. A time is recorded only where the source itself displayed one (Kitco's panel timestamp '19:43 NY Time' and its body sentence 'as of October 23, 2026, 7:42 p.m. ET').
liveCheck.noHallucinations: Blank means unverified. A source conflict is published, not resolved by preference. Inherited same-day reads are labelled with the session that actually made them. checks.sourceExcerpt: Actual fineness may not be more than three one-thousandth parts below the mark on the tested solder-free part; for the entire article including solder, seven one-thousandth parts applies to articles other than watchcases or flatware.

checks.subject: 15 USC 297 identifying trademark
checks.sourceExcerpt: Official U.S. Government Publishing Office text; the link resolved to https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title15/pdf/USCODE-2024-title15-chap8-sec297.pdf. '§ 297. Stamping plated articles'. (a) rolled gold plate / gold plate / gold filled / electroplate articles may not be stamped with any word or mark usually employed to indicate the fineness of gold 'unless such word or mark be accompanied by other words, plainly indicating that such article or part thereof is made of rolled gold plate, gold plate, or gold electroplate, or is gold filled, as the case may be'. (b) Identifying trademark: a manufacturer or dealer subject to section 294 who applies a quality mark indicating gold or silver content 'shall — (A) Apply or cause to be applied to that article a trademark of such persons, which has been duly registered or applied for registration under the laws of the United States ... or the name of such person', and each identifying trademark or name 'shall be applied to that article by the same means as that used in applying the quality mark or stamp appearing thereon, in type or lettering at least as large as that used in such quality mark or stamp, and in a position as close as possible to that quality mark or stamp.' (June 13, 1906, ch. 3289, § 4, 34 Stat. 261; Pub. L. 87-354, § 1, Oct. 4, 1961, 75 Stat. 775; Pub. L. 91-366, § 1(e), July 31, 1970, 84 Stat. 691.) The Cornell LII page for the same section remains a mirror and is named as such in the reference note.

scopeReads.subject: 16 CFR § 23.18 — Misrepresentation of weight and “total weight.”
scopeReads.sourceExcerpt: eCFR page state: 'This content is from the eCFR and is authoritative but unofficial. Displaying title 16, up to date as of 10/21/2026. Title 16 was last amended 10/19/2026.' Authority: 15 U.S.C. 45, 46. Source: 83 FR 40667, Aug. 16, 2018. Text: '(a) It is unfair or deceptive to misrepresent the weight of a diamond. (b) It is unfair or deceptive to use the word “point” or any abbreviation in any representation, advertising, marking, or labeling to describe the weight of a diamond, unless the weight is also stated as decimal parts of a carat (e.g., 25 points or .25 carat). A carat is a standard unit of weight for a diamond and is equivalent to 200 milligrams (1/5 gram). A point is one one-hundredth (1/100) of a carat.'
scopeReads.finding: § 23.18 governs DIAMOND weight representations. It does not require disclosure of a ring's gold-alloy gram weight, so the checklist no longer cites it as the basis for the grams criterion; it is cited for what it actually says, and the grams criterion is labelled as this project's buying rule.
